pitch.keziah: Everyone here is offering you a promise. Mine's hungry, and you'll hear it ask.
pitch.rook: She's the last one. Pick me and you're the second person alive who knows her name.

before: Hollin is a sworn village, a day short of the keep. Nobody in it is hungry. Nobody is fighting. Every hearth is lit, which is more than Ironwake can say. Nobody will meet my eye.
I asked a girl at the well her name. She said, "We're well, thank you," and went back to the bucket.
Past Hollin the keep is in sight across a field and a river. The rime on its walls has started to run.
(Placeholder card until the writing pass. Defeat the Sworn Captain. Each group sleeps until a fight comes within its hearing.)

The keeper at Sorrel Bend has stopped writing. Maud's order kept the lazar house there until the armistice, then called its sisters home and left the sick with him. Maud packs the basin. "The carts come at dusk. Nobody strips this door till then. You won't be thanked."

(Hold out six turns. The lanes in are announced. A unit that ends its move on the bar beside a lane, 8,1 north or 10,4 east, closes that lane for the rest of the map. The ford south cannot be barred.)
after: The carts come at dusk. They find the keeper, and the meal bins full, bought by someone who never signed the book. Maud counts the beds: forty, twelve in use. "I'm angry at the order. It won't break tonight. Who here hasn't eaten?" She says the prayer over every bed, then over the keeper, with his name in it.

before: (Bet Lowry asks for one day and three of the company. Take the old bakehouse: Bet at its oven hearth, 8,3, wins. The map is lost if she falls.)
quests.ending: Bet Lowry swore first, the one the oath could not hold, choosing it.

before: Maud is going to the first shrine, a half-day off the weir road and older than the split. No rite-keeper alive has been inside. The causeway in is trodden to mud this month. "Somebody's put a man in the door. Move him. I'm going up to the altar."
(Get Maud onto the altar at 7,0 by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if she falls. Pursuers cross the causeway at 7,6 from turn 2, announced; a unit that waits where it began its phase braces.)
after: Maud kneels at the altar and says the rite, the words in order. At the response she stops. She stays on her knees longer than any prayer takes, listening, then says the response again with one word changed. On the road back she goes down the line looking at hands, and treats the frostbite first.
(Maud carries Maud's Psalter now: a heal at range 1 to 2, bound to her. Its art, Unasked, doubles a heal on an ally who has not moved or acted, and that ally's phase ends where it stands.)

before: The shrine-school at Aldmere burned around Pell when she was fourteen. The roof never went back on, and the rain has had eight years at the shelves. Now somebody brings torches for what it left. "Whatever's dry comes out. The catalogue's chained under the lectern, so I'll know what we leave."

(Get Pell off the east edge, 12,3 to 12,5, by the end of turn 7; anyone still on the board when she exits is left behind and falls. The map is lost if she falls. Three chests hold what the fire missed. The burners come in from the west road from turn 1, announced.)
after: Pell comes out with the catalogue under her arm, the chain still hanging off it. On the road she reads it through and marks the margin beside every book that stayed behind. That night she starts on the first of them from memory.

before: Somebody came down the undercroft stair after the raid with a lamp and a can of oil. The door opens only to the garrison; Pell enlisted for that door, and has the key off the quartermaster before the captain finishes saying yes. "The stair, not the door. I want the desk read before anyone brings the oil back down."

(Get Pell onto the reading desk at 16,4 by the end of turn 7. The map is lost if she falls. The sworn come down the stair at 1,10 from turn 2, announced. Two groups sleep in the stacks and the cells; walls do not stop them hearing.)
after: The charter is cut above the reading desk in the shrine script. Pell counts the anchor rings first: more rings than chains. She reads it twice without moving her lips. At the top of the stair she tears a page from her book and puts it in the captain's hand:
Let the iron keep it from waking, and let us keep the iron.
(Pell carries Pell's Commonplace now: Cinder's numbers, bound to her, and it never catches. Its art, Read Ahead, reaches one tile further for 2 less Power.)

before: Teodor's grandfather stood watch on a hill above Aldmere for thirty years and is buried under its cairn. Sworn men have been digging there since the lambing. Teodor hears it out, then goes for his boots. "They'll have the stones off him by harvest."

(Defeat their captain on the cairn's fort at 7,0 by the end of turn 9. The map is lost if Teodor falls. The cairn's door at 7,2 is one tile wide. More come up the hill behind you from turn 3, announced.)
after: The sworn had the cairn half down and the shroud cut open at the hands, where a watchman is buried with what he carried. The hands were empty. Where Teodor leaned the lance on the cairn, frost has come up on the socket, and nowhere else on the hill. He lays the stones back one at a time before he touches it again.
(The Family Lance's last stage waited on this. It wakes once Teodor has fought enough with it, now or later.)

before: The crown's bills on Ottilie's firm were marked paid the week it went under, at a counting house on the Sallow canal. The house keeps two books: one for the guild, one for whoever pays the lock-keeper. "The guild's book says paid. If they won't sell me the other one, I'll collect. I want to know who."

(Rout: every enemy falls by the end of turn 11. The map is lost if Ottilie falls. The canal is crossed only at the bridges, 6,1 and 6,7; a bow reaches over it and a sword does not. More come up the near bank from turn 2, announced.)
after: The second book is in the strongroom. Her firm's line: received from the crown, paid out the same day, to bearer, and the Warden's seal at the foot of the page. "Hask. I had him down as honest. I'm ashamed of that." She cuts the page loose and lays it in her own ledger, under her father's last line.

before: Hask kept his own books, in a Sallow bookroom two days east: which raiders he paid, and which villages they burned for it. Nobody in the regions will believe a copy. Ottilie empties her satchel to make room. "A copy trades at a discount. I want the originals out before somebody thinks to burn them."

(Escape: Ottilie leaves by the east road, 14,3 to 14,5, by the end of turn 8; whoever is still on the board then is lost, so the ally leaves first. The map is lost if Ottilie falls. Dusk: sight is 4 on turn 1 and one less each turn, never under 1; nobody strikes what their side cannot see. Riders come down the road behind you from turn 2, announced.)
after: Ottilie sets Hask's books out on a trestle in the Sallow square. By noon there's a line. People find their villages by the date of the burning, then the sum, in his hand. A Kestrow quarryman and an Aldmere miller share one page. At dusk a guildsman asks her price for the set. She turns the page for the quarryman.
(Ottilie carries Ottilie's Tally now: the Iron Bow's numbers, bound to her. Its art, Paid in Full, looses one arrow at +6 Power and -25 Acc that never doubles.)

before: Rook asks for a day and one pair of hands. The chapter keeps its roll of seats in a house on the crag above the gorge. Her name went onto it under the extra seat, the year somebody paid for that seat. "I want to read who. They watch the bridge up there. Nobody watches the sky."

(Seize: Rook stands on the roll room, 12,1, by the end of turn 8; its one door is 12,2. The map is lost if Rook falls. A flier crosses the gorge; on foot, only the road bridge crosses the gorge. A bow crit grounds a flier; over water she then cannot move. Pursuers from turn 2, announced.)
after: The last page of the roll is the chapter's claim to the extra seat. Pinned under it, a receipt: paid in full, in new keep silver. Under that, the drake's number, and Rook's name on the line below. "Your keep bought a seat with us." She folds the receipt into her glove and leaves the roll open.
(The Drover is open to Rook at her second promotion: the other door above the Skyrider.)

before: The prison's outer gate stands a day north of Aldmere, under the hill, with the first warden's name cut over it. Hask's sworn are chipping the stone around the name for shards. Teodor knows the road: his grandfather drove sheep past it every spring. "He'd never let them drink there."

(Defeat their captain on the fort before the gate, 7,2, by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Teodor falls. The old wall at row 5 has two ways through: a one-tile gap at 4,5 and a breach at 10,5 and 11,5. Riders keep the east yard. More come up the road behind you from turn 3, announced.)
after: Over the gate the name is worn shallow, the sworn's chisel marks all round it. Teodor goes over it with a finger, letter by letter. Then he turns the lance over and scrapes the socket with his thumbnail until the same letters come up under the rust. He oils the socket that night, and the letters with it.

(The Family Lance is the First Warden's Lance now. Once woken, its art Turn the Key strikes at -4 Power, once, never doubling; a hit the enemy survives locks it, Mov 0 until its side's next phase ends, while Teodor stands beside it. If he leaves or falls, the lock drops to a chill.)

before: Keziah's mother kept a shrine on a knoll off the west road. Each region has burned it once. Now someone is stripping the lead off what is left of the roof, standing on her floor to do it. "I need one of you. Whoever packed a second blanket. I'll feed you after."
(Rout: defeat every enemy by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Keziah falls. The ring wall has a west door at 4,3 and a breach at 7,5. More come up the road from turn 3, announced.)
after: The hearthstone is cracked through. Keziah sweeps the ash off it with a bough and sets her own supper in the offering bowl. "Freezing in here. Nobody lights that, it's hers." She eats nothing and sleeps across the door.

before: Rook asks for one more day. The ledger in the rookery's loft, on the fells above the chapter house, still lists one cold drake as a holding and one rider on the line below. The roost is full of the church's wingriders. "I know every one of them by how they land. They'll follow. Let them."

(Escape: get everyone off the east edge, 14,4 to 14,6, by the end of turn 9. Rook leaving wins the map, and anyone still on the board is left behind as fallen, so Rook leaves last. The map is lost if Rook falls. On foot only the bridge at 7,5 and 8,5 crosses the ravine; an enemy bow's crit grounds Rook; over water she then cannot move. Riders from the rookery behind from turn 2, announced.)
after: Rook strikes the holding line in the loft's ledger, then her own, and leaves the pen across the page. Halfway down the fell, to the drake: "It was only us two on that page, and now there's no page, and I'm lonely, with you breathing down my neck." The drake leans on her the rest of the way.

before: Keziah knows the man on the door. Joab kept the lamps at her mother's shrine; he is sworn now, bound to the envoy Hask sent to the outland stone on the moor with a seat and a god for her people. "He'll know me, and he won't say my name. Leave him to me."

(Defeat Boss: defeat the envoy, who keeps the fort at 12,3, by the end of turn 10. The map is lost if Keziah falls. Joab holds the yard's west door at 9,4, bound to the envoy: if the envoy falls first, Joab lays down the axe, freed. A breach in the south wall at 11,7 is the long way round. More come up behind you from turn 5, announced.)
after: Hask's offer is cut into the stone's face over the old marks: a seat by the fire. Keziah reads it with her fingers, swearing at the cold of it. She says her oath over it in the outland tongue, which nobody else there speaks. Then she scrapes his letters off with the scythe's heel until the old marks show.

hires.name: Corin Ashby
hires.line: Took the bounty because the harvest failed. Says so.

hires.name: Bet Lowry
hires.line: Cooked for a garrison twenty years. Still counts heads at supper.

hires.name: Ines Tarrow
hires.line: Hunts for a living. Charges extra for people.

hires.name: Mattias Grue
hires.line: Failed out of a shrine school. Kept the books.

hires.name: Tamsin Hale
hires.line: Left her parish over a roof. Won the argument, lost the roof.

hires.name: Wat Dunmore
hires.line: Sold his horse twice. Bought it back once.

hires.name: Edda Vane
hires.line: Flew dispatches for a war that ended. Nobody wrote to tell her.
